questions.text:
Following declaration of an array of struct, assumes size of byte, short, int and long are 1,2,3 and 4 respectively. Alignment rule stipulates that n byte field must be located at an address divisible by n, the fields in the struct are not rearranged, padding is used to ensure alignment. All elements of array should be of same size.
 Struct complx
       Short s
       Byte b
       Long l
       Int i
End Complx
Complx C[10]
Assuming C is located at an address divisble by 8, what is the total size of C, in bytes?
questions.solution:
Field sizes: short 2, byte 1, long 4, int 3, each aligned to its size:
- s at 0-1, b at 2, 1 byte padding, l at 4-7
- i needs an address divisible by 3 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 9-11

For every element of the array to keep the same alignment (C starts at an 8-aligned address), the key pads each struct to 16 bytes [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 10 [latex]\times[/latex] 16 = 160 bytes.

(This question was excluded from ISRO's evaluation.)

Answer: 160

The comma operator has the lowest precedence, so x=622,100,101; is (x=622),100,101 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] x = 622.

- 622 = 0x026E. On little endian the first byte is the low byte 0x6E = 110.
- 622 % 3 = 1.

110 [latex]\times[/latex] 1 = 110

Answer: 110
